_doc: Instagram Reels plan (owner's rule, Jul 29 2026): two reels per day per
account, rotating through three shapes so the same account never posts the
same kind of video twice in one day.
Reels are built from the SAME board the morning carousel used. That is
deliberate: the fares were verified once, at 6:52, and everything posted
all day points at that one verified board. A reel never re-fetches, so it
can never show a number the carousel and the site disagree with.
ROTATION. index = (date.toordinal() * slots_per_day + slot) % 3 over the
'order' list below. Deterministic, so a rerun of the same slot rebuilds the
same reel instead of quietly switching shape mid-day, and every shape comes
up equally often across the week.
AUDIO. The Instagram content publishing API cannot attach a track from
Instagram's music library. No API can. So a reel is silent unless an audio
file is sitting in assets/reel-audio/ — drop .mp3/.m4a files there and the
renderer picks one per reel and mixes it under the video at the level in
'audio'. Until then a silent AAC track is muxed in anyway, because a video
with no audio stream at all is the kind of edge case Meta's transcoder

spotlight.caption_lead: The single biggest drop out of {origin} today.

destination.label: THREE CITIES
destination.caption_lead: Three cities from {origin}, all under their typical fare.

safe_area._doc: Instagram draws its own UI over a reel. Top ~200px carries the account row, the bottom ~430px carries caption and buttons, the right ~150px carries the action rail. Nothing that must be read goes outside this box.

limits._doc: Reels accept 3s to 15min; the algorithm rewards short and complete. Anything the renderer builds outside this range is a bug, so it fails loudly instead of uploading.
